title: Wonton Soup
description: Wonton Soup is a classic Chinese comfort dish featuring delicate handmade wontons filled with savory pork, sweet shrimp, ginger, and spring onions, served in a clear aromatic chicken broth. The combination of tender dumplings, fragrant broth, and fresh garnishes creates a refined restaurant-style soup that is light yet deeply satisfying.

ingredients.title: For the Wontons
items: Ground pork – 250 g (½ lb), preferably around 20% fat
Shrimp – 100 g, peeled, deveined, and finely chopped

ingredients.title: For the Soup Broth
items: Chicken stock – 1 liter (4 cups), preferably homemade
Dried shiitake mushrooms – 2, soaked and sliced (optional)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Preparing the Wonton Filling
steps: In a mixing bowl, combine ground pork, chopped shrimp, spring onions, grated ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil, salt, and white pepper.
Mix thoroughly until the filling becomes sticky and cohesive, which helps it hold together inside the wrappers.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Folding the Wontons
steps: Place approximately 1 tsp of filling in the center of each wonton wrapper.
Moisten the wrapper edges lightly with water.
Fold the wrapper into a triangle and press firmly to seal.
Bring the two outer corners together and press lightly to create the traditional wonton shape.
Repeat until all the filling has been used.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Preparing the Broth
steps: Place the chicken stock in a large pot and bring it to a gentle simmer.
Add ginger slices, smashed garlic, light soy sauce, sesame oil, and shiitake mushrooms if using.
Simmer gently for 10–15 minutes to infuse the broth with the aromatics.
Taste and adjust the seasoning with salt as needed.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Cooking the Wontons
steps: Bring a separate pot of water to a gentle boil.
Add the wontons in batches to prevent them from sticking together.
Cook for approximately 3–4 minutes, or until the wontons float and the filling is completely cooked.
Remove the cooked wontons with a slotted spoon and transfer them directly to warmed serving bowls.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Assembling the Soup
steps: Strain the broth if desired to remove the ginger, garlic, and mushrooms.
Pour the hot broth gently over the cooked wontons.
Garnish with chopped spring onions and fresh cilantro.
Add a few drops of chili oil for optional heat.
Serve immediately while the wontons and broth are hot.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve immediately as a light Chinese appetizer or main course.
Pair with steamed rice, fried rice, or stir-fried noodles for a more substantial meal.
Add extra spring onions, cilantro, or chili oil at the table according to preference.
For a noodle variation, serve the wontons over thin egg noodles with the aromatic broth.

chefTips: Use a clear, flavorful homemade chicken stock whenever possible for superior depth and clarity.
Do not overfill the wonton wrappers, as excessive filling can cause them to split during cooking.
Mix the pork and shrimp filling until sticky to create a cohesive texture that stays inside the wrapper.
Keep unused wonton wrappers covered with a slightly damp towel so they do not dry out while folding.
Cook wontons separately from the broth to keep the soup clear and prevent excess starch from clouding it.
The pork and shrimp combination provides a balanced blend of savory richness, sweetness, and tenderness.
Serve immediately after assembly because freshly cooked wontons have the best texture.
